assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching the 10^-18 fractional-uncertainty regime are a clear case of a measurement advance that opens new physics: the magic-wavelength lattice idea removes Doppler and recoil limits while retaining large atom numbers, and the resulting clocks test fundamental constants, enable relativistic geodesy and underpin the planned redefinition of the second. From an atomic-physics view the originality is high and the impact on measurement science is concrete and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and led its first realisation; Ye's group drove the strontium lattice clock to the 10^-18 level and many-body clock physics. The two-name configuration is clean. Other contributors (for example Hall, Hänsch on combs, or Ido and others) are already recognised or less decisive for this specific discovery.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories worldwide confirm the performance, intercomparisons exist and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, with international redefinition of the second under discussion.
uncertainties: I note a documented stay in John Hall's laboratory and that Ye's career is tied to the Hall/JILA environment; this is a potential perceived conflict I report rather than resolve.
Which ion or atomic species and which group should be credited for the final 10^-18 milestones is partly contested (for example Al+ ion clocks and Yb lattice clocks from other groups).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal made trapped-ion quantum computing a concrete, physically complete scheme, and subsequent experiments established high-fidelity entangling gates, quantum algorithms and simulation with ions. It is foundational for the quantum-information era and rests on methods of atomic physics I know well.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supply the theoretical proposal; Blatt is a leading experimental realiser of the gates and algorithms. Wineland and Haroche were already recognised in 2012 for single-quantum-system control, and other experimental leaders (for example Wineland's group, Monroe, Wineland-NIST gate work) are not in the supplied credit, so the experimental credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many independent laboratories and now commercial platforms. The foundational results are mature, though the long-term computational impact is still developing and some of it overlaps the 2012 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize may weaken the case for a separate award.
Experimental credit beyond Blatt is not supported by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED created the architecture for superconducting qubit readout, coupling and control and is the working basis of most superconducting quantum processors. It transfers cavity QED concepts, which I know from atomic physics, to engineered artificial atoms, and the strong-coupling demonstration was a decisive step.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed the circuit QED architecture and Wallraff, with Schoelkopf, demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Girvin is credited but only up to three may be chosen; I judge the proposal and first strong-coupling experiment to be best captured by these three, a choice that reflects a hard allocation decision.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and widely reproduced. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, which creates a possible near-term overlap, though circuit QED is a distinct discovery.
uncertainties: Close temporal and topical proximity to the 2025 prize.
Dropping Girvin is a judgement call on attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Mott insulator transition, single-site-resolved microscopy and controlled many-body Hamiltonians, giving a new experimental route to strongly correlated matter. It is a major, originality-rich advance in atomic physics with broad influence.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) proposed the Hubbard-model realisation, Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott insulator experiment and microscopy, and Esslinger obtained fermionic results. Restricting to three people leaves out Esslinger and Cirac, an unresolved allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent groups and a large literature; the field is long established, though the ultimate advantage of simulators is still being demonstrated.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on bosonic Mott physics or on microscopy and fermions.
Overlap in names with the trapped-ion and Rydberg candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry provides inertial and gravitational sensors, tests of the equivalence principle and measurement of constants with exceptional precision, embodying the idea that technical progress is limited by what can be measured and how accurately. The concept builds on laser cooling and coherent manipulation and is a significant, original instrument.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich (with Chu) made decisive early contributions; Chu was already a laureate in 1997 for laser cooling, which may complicate allocation. Schmiedmayer is also credited but is not selected. The three-way split of early priority is partly unclear.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with many demonstrations, including gravimeters and gradiometers; fundamental-physics reach and practical impact remain growing rather than complete.
uncertainties: Overlap with Chu's earlier recognition and the unclear priority of Bordé versus Kasevich-Chu.
Not yet a decisive fundamental discovery as opposed to a technique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays with optical tweezers use blockade interactions for quantum simulation and gate operations, and have produced notable many-body states and early error-corrected logical operations. It is highly significant for neutral-atom quantum technology and an area close to my own expertise.
assessment.attribution: Credited names include five people; Lukin and Browaeys led decisive array experiments, Saffman the blockade gate proposals and experiments, and Zoller and Grangier made foundational blockade proposals. Choosing three is a hard compromise and the credit is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing and independently reproduced, but still in rapid development, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the longer-established atomic-physics candidates.
Five credited names cannot fit within three laureates; allocation unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution founded quantum cryptography with the BB84 protocol and the entanglement-based E91 protocol, linking quantum-foundations concepts to secure communication; a lasting and conceptually original contribution.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are clearly decisive through BB84. Ekert's independent entanglement-based proposal also merits credit; the longlist includes two spellings of his name, and I use the form Artur K. Ekert. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Experiments and commercial systems exist for decades, so it is mature, though security proofs and practical-device loopholes mean real-world impact is still evolving. The 2022 prize on entanglement already touched this territory.
uncertainties: Duplicate spellings of Ekert's name in the credited list.
Possible overlap with the 2022 prize and incomplete credit to Wiesner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond opened room-temperature solid-state quantum sensing and spin-qubit research; the scheme uses optical pumping and readout familiar from atomic physics and has wide applications from nanoscale magnetometry to biology.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-spin optical detection and coherent control; Lukin advanced sensing and multi-qubit registers. Other groups (for example Hanson, Awschalom) contributed to the broader field, so the configuration is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups, with a strong sensing literature; broader quantum-network applications are still maturing.
uncertainties: Compound discovery in which detection, control and sensing may need different recognition.
Overlap with B033 on optical access to spins, which I did not rank.
